_source: docs/eras/uv.md, '15. Powder bed printer' and line 15 'Printed parts' (package UV-A8). Real: electrode induction-melting gas atomisation (ALD's EIGA atomisers), laser powder bed fusion, hot isostatic pressing, NASA's RAMPT printed rocket chambers.
_how_it_is_used: Read by server_scripts/grindless/uv/materials.js (one gtceu:powder_bed_fusion atomise row per metal, one print and one press row per part, ids grindless:powder_bed_fusion/<atomise|print|press>_<name>) and by tools/analysis/test/uv-materials.test.mjs. Nothing here is repeated in code.
atomise: circuit 1. ingots in -> the same number of powders out; argonIn of the metal's argon goes in, argonBack comes back (the rest stays in the powder's pores).

print: the programmed circuit is the part's; powderIn powders and the fibre laser module go in, the near-net part and powderBack powders (the unsintered bed sieved with its spatter) come out. The module is a chanced input at moduleWear (of 10,000) and the worn module comes out at the same chance (2 % wear, as the laser fusion chamber).
press: circuit 3. the near-net part + argon -> the finished part + all the argon back (hot isostatic pressing).

metals[]: name, ingot (GTM's), powder (F1's grindless:<metal>_am_powder). parts[]: name, metal, circuit (2 for the GTM parts, 4-6 for the parts GTM lacks), powderIn, powderBack (net powderIn - powderBack: 3 for a GTM gear or rotor, 75 % of GTM's 4 ingots), nearNet, output, gtm (true: a cheaper route to a GTM part, not counted for rule 7).

parts.name: thruster_chamber
parts._why: The ion thruster's regeneratively cooled chamber (machine 17): one piece with its cooling channels, which no GTM recipe makes.

parts.name: array_mount
parts._why: The launcher's laser array mount (machine 23): neutronium does not creep under the array's heat.

parts.name: probe_frame
parts._why: The probes' printed frame (penetrator and precursor probes): a lattice too light to machine.

parts.name: rhea_impeller
parts._why: UIV-A8, line 6: the UIV pump's impeller, one piece with its curved blades; the RHEA's atomised powder (the metals entry above) is printed, then HIPed at the megabar press.

parts.name: w_mesh
parts._why: UIV-A9, line 29: the capillary porous mesh of the divertor, printed from the RHEA powder (no tungsten powder exists), then wetted with Li-Sn.
